note: Curated GOLD for the metastore GDWIKI oracle (nDCG + recall@k), dogfooded on keryx's OWN .metaproject/wiki/ corpus. Each query closely paraphrases the `## Summary` / opening paragraph of exactly one wiki page, chosen so its relevance is OBVIOUS and no other page in the corpus is about the same subject; only that one page id is hand-labeled relevant per query. The gold targets keryx's four distinctive architecture pages (os-sandbox, project-map, testing-map, quality-map), whose summaries carry real prose; component pages are deliberately avoided because their auto-generated `groups N file(s), depends on ...` summaries are near-templated and make retrieval relevance ambiguous (see docs/requirements/keryx-benchmark-suite/metrics-and-validation.md). A `passage` here is a whole wiki page (the retrieval unit `keryx wiki ask` cites; there is no sub-page passage granularity). Shape matches the AffectedSetFile the CLI already loads: `target` is the query, `affected` is the gold passage id list (the ranked citation `path`s `keryx wiki ask` emits, e.g. `wiki/architecture/os-sandbox.md`), plus a `justification` carried for audit (not consumed by the loader). The gold and the separate hand-labeled groundedness (wiki-groundedness.json) are NEVER regenerated by the producer script.

targets.target: OS sandbox kernel-enforced containment refuses a run when it cannot contain the process
targets.justification: Paraphrases os-sandbox.md's summary verbatim ("kernel-enforced containment layer ... When containment cannot be applied, a run is refused, never silently downgraded"); no other wiki page concerns the OS sandbox.

targets.target: macOS Seatbelt and Linux bubblewrap constrain which paths secrets and network a running process can reach
targets.justification: Paraphrases os-sandbox.md's summary mechanism verbatim ("using macOS Seatbelt (sandbox-exec) or Linux bubblewrap (bwrap) ... which paths it can write, which secrets it can read, and which network it can reach"); a second, independent facet of the same page, no other page names Seatbelt/bubblewrap.

targets.target: deterministic architecture map of the repository as a graph of code files and assets with import relationships between top-level modules
targets.justification: Paraphrases project-map.md's summary verbatim ("the deterministic architecture map for the project ... a graph of code files and assets, including import relationships between top-level modules"); no other page is the repository code-graph map.

targets.target: high-level map of the project's testing infrastructure framework test scripts and configuration files
targets.justification: Paraphrases testing-map.md's summary verbatim ("a high-level map of the project's testing infrastructure ... the testing framework in use, the available test scripts, configuration files"); no other page is the testing map.

targets.target: architecture-level quality map generated from a Code Health scan snapshot of codebase health risk and findings
targets.justification: Paraphrases quality-map.md's opening paragraph verbatim ("the architecture-level quality map for the project ... automatically generated from a Code Health scan ... a snapshot of the current codebase health, risk, and the distribution of findings"); no other page is the quality map. quality-map.md has no `## Summary` block, so only its title is lexically scored — an honest retrieval weakness this query exposes (it lands at rank 2 behind project-map, giving nDCG < 1 while recall@5 stays 1).
